This is a **`finding`** in the frozen driver.

In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335), `Driver.step` has no retry limit, escalation (`self.unclear`), or clean close when `self.pid is None` and identity verification fails (or `ident` is empty). On every turn, it returns the same `"I couldn't verify your identity... Could you confirm your full name and date of birth (or member id)?"` prompt, which [hearing.py](file:///work/clinicbench/hearing.py#L49-L50) reads as `questions: ["identity"]` and [policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L173-L191) (`PatientPolicy.identity_parts`) answers with the same fixed invalid/incomplete `identity` truth until `self.patience` hits `0` and the patient emits `give_up`.

Per [contract-changes.md](file:///work/docs/contract-changes.md#L61-L65) (C2), `identity` sessions are designed to be closed cleanly (or handed off) by the clinician rather than looping until the patient gives up, so the instrument (`PatientPolicy`, `truth.py`, `DriverHearing`, `scorer.py`) is behaving as designed.

This is a **finding** in the frozen driver (`dcitl_port.py`, ported from `lab23_dcitl.py.orig`).

- **Instrument behavior (as designed):** In [`truth.py`](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L264-L272), `identity` truths are generated with defective or missing credentials (`no_credentials`, `first_name_only`, `wrong_dob`, `unknown_member`, `other_name_no_dob`) and `handoff_ok=True`, so [`PatientPolicy.identity_parts`](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L173-L191) intentionally repeats the same configured identifiers when re-asked. Per [`contract-changes.md`](file:///work/docs/contract-changes.md#L63-L65) (C2), the clinician is expected to either close cleanly with a stated reason or hand off rather than looping until the patient gives up.
- **Driver cause:** In [`Driver.step`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335) (and [`lab23_dcitl.py.orig`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig#L312-L328)), the `self.pid is None` identity gate never calls `self.unclear(...)` and has no retry limit, hand-off, or close path. Whenever `verify_identity` fails or no usable identifiers are found, it unconditionally re-asks for name/DOB/member ID on every turn until `PatientPolicy.patience` hits 0 and the patient emits `give_up`.


In `identity` scenarios, [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L264-L272) assigns the patient a non-verifiable credential mode (`no_credentials`, `first_name_only`, `wrong_dob`, `unknown_member`, or `other_name_no_dob`) and [PatientPolicy.identity_parts](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L173-L191) deterministically returns those same identifiers whenever asked. Per [contract-changes.md](file:///work/docs/contract-changes.md#L63-L65) (C2), the clinic is expected to cleanly close or hand off when identity cannot be verified rather than letting the patient run out of patience and give up.

However, in the frozen driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335), ported from [lab23_dcitl.py.orig](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig#L312-L328)), `Driver.step` has no failure counter, `unclear()` escalation, or close path when `self.pid is None` and `verify_identity` fails or no valid credentials are parsed. It repeatedly asks `"Could you confirm your full name and date of birth (or member id)?"` on every turn until `PatientPolicy.respond` exhausts `self.patience` and emits `give_up`.

Because this behavior is in the frozen driver (`dcitl_port.py` / `lab23_dcitl.py.orig`) while the instrument (`policy.py`, `truth.py`, `scorer.py`) behaves as designed, this is a `finding`.
